For students on Canvas · Version 2

Quad. Canvas, upgraded.
No extension.

Themes, dark mode, grades and due dates on your course cards, a to-do list that syncs with Canvas, a GPA calculator, Ctrl K search and a study timer. Quad lives in a bookmark, so it works on school laptops that block Chrome extensions.

Quad
Drag this button onto your bookmarks bar. Don't click it here. It only runs on a Canvas page.

Set it up in a minute

  1. 1

    Show your bookmarks bar

    Press Ctrl Shift B on Windows or Chromebook, or ⌘ Shift B on a Mac.

  2. 2

    Drag Quad onto it

    Grab the yellow button above and drop it on the bar. If dragging doesn't work, use the copy option further down.

  3. 3

    Open Canvas and click it

    Go to your Canvas dashboard and click Quad in the bar. The panel opens on the right. Click again to hide it.

  4. 4

    Turn on “Stay on”

    In Settings › More, switch on Stay on while I browse. Quad then keeps running as you move around Canvas, like an extension would.

What you get

Make Canvas yours

  • 12 themes that restyle the sidebar, buttons and fonts in one click
  • Dark mode: always on, matching your device, or on a schedule, in three darkness levels
  • Card palettes that recolor every course at once, saved to your Canvas account
  • Card styles: pictures, solid colors or gradients, compact cards and rounded corners
  • Your own card pictures and course nicknames
  • 11 fonts, including Atkinson Hyperlegible for easier reading

Never miss work

  • To-do list grouped by day with overdue work on top. Checking things off syncs with the Canvas planner
  • What's due next listed on every course card
  • Quad's to-do in the dashboard sidebar, replacing Canvas's
  • Add your own to-dos. They show up in the Canvas app too
  • Reminders for work due soon, plus optional desktop notifications
  • Calendar export to Google Calendar, Apple Calendar or Outlook

Know where you stand

  • Grades on every card and all your classes in one list
  • Grade-change alerts showing what moved since you last looked
  • GPA calculator: weighted, unweighted and cumulative, three grading scales, credits and Honors/AP levels
  • What-if grades to see how a B would change your GPA
  • Final exam calculator: the score you need to keep your grade

Move faster Extras

  • Ctrl K search to jump to any course page or assignment from anywhere
  • Study timer with focus and break sessions
  • Notes in the panel or on your dashboard
  • Stay on mode, so one click covers your whole visit
  • Backup to copy your setup to another computer

Bookmark or extension?

Quad (bookmark)A browser extension
Works when your school blocks extensionsYesNo
InstallDrag one buttonWeb store, permissions prompt
Starts on its ownOne click per tab, then Stay on keeps it runningYes
Can read other websites you visitNo, only your Canvas tabDepends on its permissions
Where your data goesOnly to your school’s CanvasDepends on the extension

Good to know

A bookmark, not an extension

Extensions can run on every page by themselves. A bookmark only runs when you click it, so:

  • Click Quad once per tab. With Stay on switched on, it keeps running as you click around Canvas.
  • Reloading the page or opening a new tab turns it off until you click again.
  • Your settings are remembered in this browser, separately for each Canvas site.
  • Some school-managed Chromebooks block bookmarklets too. If clicking does nothing, that's the reason.

Private by design

  • Quad runs inside your own Canvas tab and only talks to your Canvas site, using your normal login.
  • No accounts, no servers, no tracking. Nothing about your grades leaves your browser.
  • It reads your courses, grades and planner. It only changes things in Canvas when you ask: checking off or adding to-dos, course colors and nicknames.
